candidates.label: IgG4-related disease (IgG4-RD) involving the right paranasal sinuses and orbital apex, with secondary bacterial sinusitis (Streptococcus constellatus) and optic neuropathy
missing_or_uncertain: Fibrosis and obliterative phlebitis not mentioned

candidates.label: Invasive fungal sinusitis (e.g., mucormycosis) with orbital apex syndrome
missing_or_uncertain: No fungal culture or histopathology evidence

candidates.label: Granulomatosis with polyangiitis (Wegener's) with sinus and orbital involvement
Sinonasal lymphoma (e.g., extranodal NK/T-cell lymphoma) with orbital extension
missing_or_uncertain: No atypical lymphoid cells or necrosis described
IgG4 elevation not typical for lymphoma

candidates.label: Acute bacterial sinusitis with orbital cellulitis and optic nerve compression
missing_or_uncertain: IgG4 elevation unexplained by infection alone

response.rationale: The combination of elevated serum IgG4, dense IgG4-positive plasma cell infiltrate, sinus opacification with bony erosion, and orbital apex involvement strongly supports IgG4-related disease. The positive Streptococcus constellatus culture likely represents secondary bacterial infection. Other differentials such as invasive fungal sinusitis, GPA, lymphoma, and acute bacterial sinusitis are less consistent with the plasma cell-rich pathology and IgG4 elevation.
